v: The result of humility and the fear of the LORD is wealth, honor, and life.
b: This passage reveals an eternal truth: when we fear God with a humble heart, we gain not only material abundance but, more importantly, spiritual honor and a full life. Humility is not self-deprecation; it is a true recognition of our own place, and an acknowledgment of and respect for God’s limitless power.

Think of how a tree begins to grow from a seed. The seed in the soil seems unremarkable, yet holds enormous potential. When the seed is humbly buried in the earth, it begins to sprout and gradually grows into a magnificent tree. In the end the tree not only bears fruit, but offers shade, and becomes an indispensable part of the ecosystem. In the same way, when we keep a humble heart and fear Yahweh in life, our lives will also bear abundant fruit, enriching not only ourselves but those around us.

A successful entrepreneur became wealthy and respected through his innovative business model. He never took credit proudly, but always kept learning and improving humbly. His company culture encouraged every employee to keep learning and respected every opinion, and it was this culture that shaped an innovative and inclusive working environment, driving the company forward. His story tells us that reverence and humility are not only personal cultivation but the key to leadership and innovation.

Dear friends, when we choose to fear God with a humble heart, every challenge in life becomes a chance to grow, and every failure becomes an accumulation of wisdom. This way of life leads us to true wealth, honor, and fullness of life.
ah: Proverbs 22:4 gives a profound insight: fearing Yahweh and having a humble heart bring abundant life, honor, and real wealth. This verse teaches us that true blessing comes from reverence for God and humility of heart. Here are concrete ways we can practice this teaching in daily life:
a: **Develop a Sense of Reverence for God**
Spend time each day in prayer and Bible reading, letting God’s Word be the guide for your life. Through a deep understanding of God’s words, build reverence for God’s authority.
**Practice Humble Interactions**

In your dealings with family, friends, and colleagues, practice listening more than speaking, respect others’ opinions, and be willing to accept their advice. This shows humility and also helps build more harmonious relationships.
**Openly Admit Your Shortcomings**
When you meet failure at work or in social settings, be brave enough to admit mistakes and learn from them. Such conduct not only promotes personal growth but is a practical expression of humility.
**Service and Giving**

Look for opportunities to serve in the community or church, whether through volunteer activities or helping those in need. Service is not only an expression of reverence for God but a practice of the humble life.
**A Thankful Attitude**

Keep a thankful heart, thanking God for everything He gives, including daily provision, the company of family and friends, and every opportunity in life. Gratitude makes the heart more humble and helps us treasure God’s gifts more.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, we thank You for teaching us through Your Word to fear You and keep a humble heart. We ask that You help us keep practicing these teachings in daily life, whether through prayer, service, or our dealings with others. May our lives keep reflecting reverence for You and a humble attitude, so that in Your grace we may gain true wealth, honor, and life. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you find true wealth, glory, and life in reverence and humility. May your life be a fertile field that keeps bearing good fruit. Amen!

v: doing nothing through rivalry or through conceit, but in humility, each counting others better than himself;
b: This passage stresses the power of humility and teaches us to avoid vanity and selfish behavior. In a society that increasingly values personal achievement and surface polish, this is a timely and important reminder: true worth comes from how we respect and lift others, not merely from promoting ourselves.

Think of a football team. In a match, if every player cares only about his own goals and performance rather than the strategy and success of the whole team, then however talented they are, the team will find it hard to win. But when everyone counts teammates as more important than himself, when they pass the ball selflessly, support one another, and face their opponents together, the whole team becomes stronger and more likely to win the game.

This image of team spirit can be applied to our families, workplaces, and even communities. When we stop fighting for personal attention and praise and begin to truly care for and support those around us, we not only lift others, but enrich our own lives.

A community leader devoted himself to improving the quality of life of low-income families. He might have chosen to put himself in the spotlight and enjoy all the praise. But he chose the path of humility, crediting his success to his team and the cooperation of the community. This attitude not only increased the impact of the project, but also encouraged more volunteers to join in, because they knew their contributions would be treasured and recognized.

Dear family, when we choose humility and put others before ourselves, we find true honor in God’s eyes. This is not submission or hypocrisy, but the recognition that all of us are precious lives created by God, and everyone deserves respect and care.
ah: Philippians 2:3 reminds us to avoid rivalry and vain conceit, and instead, in humility, to count others better than ourselves. This teaching guides us in how to relate to others in daily life with the mind of Christ. Here are several concrete ways to practice the teaching of this verse:
a: **Cultivate the Habit of Appreciating Others**
At work or in community activities, actively look for opportunities to praise others’ achievements and strengths. This not only encourages others but helps you develop a thankful and humble heart.
**Avoid a Spirit of Comparison and Competition**
On social media and in daily life, avoid comparing yourself with others. Focus on your own growth and progress, rather than striving for a better position or recognition than others.
**Practice Teamwork and Cooperation**
At work or in church service, actively seek cooperation rather than competition. Offer help, accept others’ opinions and help, and reach goals together.
**Stay Humble in Conflict**
When facing disagreement and conflict, listen and respond with humility and understanding, and seek a peaceful solution rather than insisting on who is right or wrong.
**Reflect on and Adjust Your Motives**
Regularly reflect on the motives behind your actions, making sure they are not for personal glory or recognition. Ask God to help you adjust your attitude, so that in everything you may glorify Him.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for teaching us through Your Word how to be humble in mind and to regard others as better than ourselves. We ask that You help us practice this teaching in our daily interactions, whether in the family, at work, or at church. Keep our hearts far from rivalry and vanity, and let us seek the true glory that comes from serving and loving our neighbor as ourselves. Help us look at and treat those around us every day with the mind of Christ. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you find strength in a humble mind and see the worth of others, and may you, in lifting others up, lift your own soul. Amen!

v: Finally, all of you be like-minded, compassionate, loving as brothers, tenderhearted, courteous,
b: This passage is a beautiful reminder for our daily conduct, teaching us how to live with others in love and humility in this diverse world. It calls us to care not only for our own needs, but even more for the feelings of others, and to treat people with brotherly and sisterly love.

Think of a tree. It is made up of many different parts: roots, trunk, branches, and leaves. Each part has its own unique role and function, but they must all live together in harmony for the whole tree to thrive. The roots go deep into the soil and steady the trunk; the trunk supports the branches and leaves; the leaves, through photosynthesis, nourish the whole tree. The success of each part depends on the health and function of the others.

So it is in our relationships. When we choose to be tenderhearted and humble, working together in unity, we are like the parts of that tree, supporting one another and growing together. Our communities, families, and workplaces can all become stronger and more harmonious because of this attitude of supporting and sympathizing with one another.

An office manager worked hard every day to make sure every employee felt valued and supported. He focused not only on performance but on building a supportive working environment, encouraging employees to share each other’s challenges and successes. This style of management not only raised the team’s overall performance, but fostered a more open and mutually helpful working atmosphere.
Dear family, when we choose to face daily life with a humble heart, we can create an environment full of love and compassion, bringing blessing not only to ourselves but to everyone around us.
ah: 1 Peter 3:8 gives us a precious reminder to be of one mind in our relationships, sympathetic, loving as brothers, and to keep a tenderhearted and humble spirit. This is the foundation for living together in harmony and promoting spiritual growth. Here are concrete ways to practice these teachings in daily life:
a: **Cultivate Empathy**
In your dealings with others, strive to understand their feelings and circumstances. This means listening more than speaking, thinking about others’ needs, and offering appropriate support.
**Strengthen Relationships in Family and Church**
Take an active part in family and church, promoting an inclusive and supportive environment. This includes joining family and church activities regularly and offering help when needed.
**Practice Selfless Love**
Love others unconditionally, especially those who seem hard to love. This love seeks no return; it is purely giving.
**Practice Humble Communication**
In conversation, avoid arrogant or self-centered language. Replace criticism with more affirmation and encouragement, which will help build more positive relationships.
**Offer Generous Service**

At work or in the community, look for opportunities to serve others. This might be through volunteering, charitable giving, or simply small acts in daily life, such as helping a neighbor with a difficult task.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for reminding us through Your Word to treat one another with humble hearts, work together in unity, and look at each other with love and compassion. We ask that You help us embody these qualities in our interactions every day, whether in the family, at work, or in the community. Give us hearts willing to serve, willing to listen, and willing to give, so that we can grow in Your love and pass it on to others. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you find strength in being of one mind, and love and sympathize with others with a tenderhearted and humble spirit. Amen!

v: Whoever therefore humbles himself as this little child is the greatest in the Kingdom of Heaven.
b: These words come from our Lord, reminding us that humility is not only a virtue but the key to entering the Kingdom of Heaven. The humility of a child lies in their innocence, directness, and dependence; they are naturally free of vanity and the spirit of competition.

A little child is playing in the sand by the sea. He is focused on the present, building a sandcastle with a small shovel and bucket. For him, every attempt is an exploration, and whatever the result, he enjoys it. When a wave knocks the castle down, he is not discouraged, but starts the next one at once. This attitude reflects an extremely important philosophy of life: enjoy the process, do not fear failure, and always keep a mind that learns and grows.

We can apply this childlike attitude to every area of life. At work, when we face challenge and pressure, if we explore the possibilities with a child’s heart, we will solve problems more creatively and flexibly. In relationships, when we treat others with an open and accepting heart, we will build deeper and more genuine connections.

A teacher taught with a child’s enthusiasm, and every day found new inspiration and new teaching methods in his students’ questions and curiosity. His classroom was always full of life, because he let students express themselves freely and drew innovation from their unpolished ideas. This way of teaching not only sparked the students’ enthusiasm for learning, but kept him with a heart that never grows old.

Dear family, let us all learn lessons from children and receive each lesson of life with a humble heart. When we do this, we will grow spiritually and take firm steps on our journey toward the kingdom of heaven.
ah: Matthew 18:4 gives us a powerful message, encouraging us to humble ourselves like a little child. In this verse, Jesus lifts up the qualities of a child as the model for the Kingdom of Heaven. Here are several practical ways to help us live out this humble attitude in daily life:
a: **Embrace an Attitude of Learning**

Children are always full of curiosity and a hunger to learn about new things. We can imitate this attitude, constantly seeking to grow in knowledge and understanding, whether spiritual, professional, or in personal interests.
**Show Dependence and Trust**
As a child depends on his parents, we should learn to depend on God and trust His plan and timing, even in uncertain or difficult times.
**Keep Innocence**
Children usually have no prejudice, and they see the world and others with clear eyes. We should strive to remove preconceptions and treat others with a pure heart.
**Practice Selfless Love**
A child’s love is direct and unconditional. We should try to express this kind of love, treating family, friends, and community members without counting the return, focusing only on giving.
**Be Quick to Forgive**
Children soon forget a quarrel and go back to playing with their friends. We should learn to forgive others’ wrongs, holding no grudges and welcoming them back with an open heart.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for reminding us through Your Word to be humble like little children. We ask that You give us pure and open hearts, and help us keep an attitude of learning in daily life, depend on You, and love those around us selflessly. Let us show Your love and glory in this world like little children. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you find the true meaning and joy of life in keeping a humble heart. Amen!

v: Likewise, you younger ones, be subject to the elder. Yes, all of you clothe yourselves with humility and subject yourselves to one another; for “God resists the proud, but gives grace to the humble.”
b: This verse teaches us the importance of humility and submission, not only respect for our elders, but an attitude we should keep toward one another in our daily lives. This humility is not weakness, but a kind of strength, the strength of being open to accepting the guidance and support of others.

Think of warriors of old. Their armor was heavy, but the most important thing was the belt around their waist, which kept their equipment fastened and let them stay agile and ready in battle. This is similar to the idea of clothing ourselves with humility: it lets us stay flexible in the challenges of life and ready to receive God’s guidance.

A young new employee joined a company, and he realized that the key to success was learning and gaining knowledge from experienced colleagues. He chose to learn with humility, listening actively and accepting advice and criticism. Over time, this young employee not only improved his skills, but won the respect and trust of his colleagues through his willingness to learn.

This story tells us that, whether at work or in the family and community, submitting to one another with a mindset of being clothed in humility can build stronger relationships, create greater harmony, and open the door to success.

Dear family, let us dress ourselves with humility every day, ready to receive the wisdom and grace that come from all around us. When we do, we will not only grow personally, but also promote the prosperity of our community.
ah: 1 Peter 5:5 reminds us that whether the young submit to the elders or all submit to one another, it should be based on humility. This verse not only emphasizes order in society and the church, but also emphasizes humility as the core of Christian character. Here are several concrete ways to practice this teaching:
a: **Respect and Submission**
In the family, workplace, and church, respect those with more experience or a higher position than yourself. Even when you disagree, express your views in a respectful way.
**Practice a Spirit of Mutual Service**
Humility is not only submission to authority, but also serving one another in daily life. Whatever our position, we should look for chances to help and support others.
**Avoid Arrogance**
Stay modest in the face of achievement, remembering that all success and talent come from God. Share the glory with others and sincerely appreciate their success.
**Actively Learn and Accept Guidance**
Seek guidance and be willing to learn from others, whether life wisdom or professional skills. Be willing to listen to and accept constructive criticism.
**Take Christ as Your Example**
Think about how Jesus Christ showed humility in His earthly ministry, and take Him as your example. When you face challenge or are misunderstood, keep a humble and gracious attitude.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for teaching us through Your Word to clothe ourselves with humility and submit to one another. Give us humble hearts, so that we can practice a spirit of respect, submission, and service at every level of life. Help us learn from the example of Jesus and keep a humble attitude in any situation. Enable us to show Your love and grace through our words and deeds. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you grow in humility, and discover the grace God gives as you submit to one another. Amen!

v: serving the Lord with all humility, with many tears, and with trials which happened to me by the plots of the Jews;
b: This passage makes us think about the true meaning of serving the Lord, and the role humility plays in the journey of faith. Facing persecution and hardship, the apostle Paul showed by his humility and perseverance his unconditional faith and love for the Lord.

A captain is sailing through a storm. The waves are fierce and the wind is strong, but the captain must stay calm and face the challenge with wisdom and a humble heart, guiding the ship to sail safely. This captain knows that each of his decisions concerns not only his own life but the safety of the whole crew. His humility comes from awe at the power of nature and from selfless commitment to a successful voyage.

This story reflects the spirit of Paul. Even in the face of hostility and threats, he still insisted on serving the Lord humbly, willing to bear personal suffering for the spread of the gospel. His tears were not only for his own suffering, but for his concern for those souls who had not yet received salvation.

We can learn from Paul’s example that true humility does not mean weakness, but is a display of courage. It requires us to lay down self and hold to justice and kindness even in adversity. In our communities, work, and families, when we choose to live with a humble heart, we can resolve conflicts in a more harmonious and compassionate way and support one another.

Dear family, let us all learn from Paul’s example, and whatever difficulty or challenge we face, serve the Lord and one another with a humble heart. In this way we can become not only better Christians, but better people.
ah: Acts 20:19 offers a profound testimony. The apostle Paul describes how in serving the Lord he showed great humility, and even under the plots of the Jews and many trials, he kept a serving heart. This passage shows us that we can keep an attitude of humility and service even in difficulty and persecution. Here are some concrete ways to practice this teaching:
a: **Continual Service**
Whatever the outside circumstances, keep looking for opportunities to serve in the church and community. Service is not limited to material giving; it includes time, attention, and care.
**Keep a Humble Mindset**
In service, stay modest, not seeking others’ praise or reward, but serving out of love for the Lord and sincere care for others.
**Keep Your Faith in Adversity**
When you face trials or persecution, learn from Paul’s example, responding with tears and firm faith, showing the perseverance and grace a Christian should have.
**Humility in Handling Conflict**
When you meet conflict in the church or family, seek reconciliation with a humble heart, even though you may have been treated unjustly or misunderstood.
**Learn to Express Emotion**

Paul mentions “many tears,” which reminds us that genuine expression of feeling in service is also important. This is not a sign of weakness, but deep empathy for the pain of others and a serious attitude toward the mission of service.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for teaching us through Paul’s example how to stay humble in service, not changing our purpose even in difficulty and trial. Give us strength and courage, so that in all circumstances we can serve You and those around us with humble hearts. When we face challenge and persecution, help us keep a firm faith and a forgiving heart. Make our lives a witness to Your love and kindness. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you find strength in humility, and whatever trials you face, hold on to your faith and service. Amen!

v: Before destruction the heart of man is proud, but before honor is humility.
b: This passage deeply reminds us that before reaching honor, we must first learn humility. It tells us that true achievement comes from inner growth and self-reflection, not from outward glory or praise.

There is a great mountain whose high peak draws climbers, but before they reach the summit they must go along winding paths and overcome all kinds of difficulties. These challenges require climbers to stay humble, to learn from each lesson, and to respect the power of nature. It is this humble attitude that finally brings them to the top, to enjoy true honor.

We can see the practical application of this principle in the story of a scientist. Early in his research career he faced major challenges. Every failed experiment made him more humble; he did not give up because of setbacks, but kept learning and adapting, and in the end his discovery changed the face of the whole scientific world. His achievement came after continual humble learning and effort.

This story tells us that whatever our goal, whether success in a career, harmony in family relationships, or personal growth, humility is a process we must go through. Only when we learn to bow our heads, accept lessons, and respect others and our environment can we truly gain honor.
Dear family, let us work every day to become more humble people, remembering that on the road to honor, humility is our indispensable companion.
ah: Proverbs 18:12 reminds us deeply that before honor comes, we must keep a humble attitude. This wisdom teaches us that before we gain any success or position, we should stay low-key and modest, because pride often leads to a fall. Here are several concrete ways to practice this humility in daily life:
a: **Self-Assessment**
Regularly reflect on your conduct and attitudes, making sure they do not come from pride or complacency. Admit your limits, and thank God and those around you for their support and help.
**Publicly Acknowledge Others**

When you achieve something at work or in the community, publicly acknowledge those who helped you along the way. This shows that you recognize that success is the result of teamwork, not something done independently.
**Avoid Boasting**
Even when your performance is outstanding, avoid boasting in front of others. Keep the focus of the conversation on the team’s or others’ contributions rather than your personal achievements.
**Accept and Seek Guidance**
Whatever your position, be willing to learn from others. Accepting guidance and drawing knowledge from it shows your humility and willingness to learn.
**Stay Humble in the Face of Criticism**
When facing criticism or feedback, accept it with an open and humble attitude, even if you do not entirely agree. This can help you grow and improve.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for reminding us through Your Word to stay humble before honor comes. We ask that You help us practice this lesson in daily life, keeping a humble heart at all times and in all places. Let us recognize that all honor and ability come from You, and teach us to be humble first before receiving any honor. When we meet challenge and trial, help us remember that humility is the road to true honor. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you find wisdom in humility and strength in learning. May you keep a humble heart, full of grace, on the road to honor. Amen!

v: LORD, you have heard the desire of the humble. You will prepare their heart. You will cause your ear to hear,
b: This verse deeply reminds us that God not only knows our needs, but cares for those who seek Him with a humble heart. He not only hears our voice; He actively takes part in the process of preparing our hearts, so that we can receive His response and blessing.

Think of how a gardener carefully tends a garden. He knows the needs of each plant, when to fertilize, when to prune, and when to water. These plants may not be able to express their needs in words, but through observation and experience the gardener understands every tiny change in them. In the same way, God knows our inner desires and needs, even before we open our mouths.

A teacher prepared lesson plans for her students every day, and spent time understanding each student’s learning style and struggles in their studies. When students ran into difficulty, she not only offered extra help, but also encouraged them to believe in their own abilities. This teacher’s conduct reflected a humble spirit of service; she focused on the students’ needs and prepared their hearts to receive learning, just as God prepares and hears our desires.

This story encourages us that whatever our role in life, we can imitate God’s care and preparation for the humble. When we treat those around us with an open and humble heart, we can not only serve them better, but also feel God’s presence and guidance in the process.
Dear family, let us strive every day to be humble people, constantly seeking God’s leading and help. When we do, we will experience more fully His love and grace toward us.
ah: Psalm 10:17 reminds us that Yahweh not only knows the desire of the humble, but prepares their hearts and listens to their prayers. This is an encouragement for us, assuring us that whatever our situation, our hearts’ cry is heard by God. Here are several concrete ways to practice this teaching:
a: **Pray Sincerely**
Spend time each day praying to God, not only asking God to meet our needs, but seeking that God’s will and leading be fulfilled in our lives.
**Cultivate a Humble Heart**
In daily life, keep reflecting on your attitudes and conduct, making sure we seek God’s guidance with a humble heart and accept His training and shaping.
**Take an Active Part in Church and Community Activities**
By joining in the church’s corporate prayer and service projects, practice a life of humble service, joining your own needs with the needs of the larger community.
**Learn Patience and Persistent Prayer**
While waiting for God’s answer, be patient, trusting that God’s timing is always best. Even when it seems there is no response, keep trusting in God’s goodness and all-knowing wisdom.
**Listen Sensitively for God’s Voice**
Through Bible reading, meditation, and prayer, draw your heart closer to God and listen sensitively to His guidance for your life and decisions.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, we thank You that You always listen to the desires of the humble. We ask that You help us cultivate sincere and humble hearts, so that our requests are in line with Your will. As we wait for Your answer, give us patience and faith, believing that You are always listening and responding to our cry. Let us rely on You more each day, and in both good times and bad bear witness to Your faithfulness and grace. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you find strength in humility, and in each of your prayers feel God’s ear inclined to you. Amen!

v: For the LORD takes pleasure in his people. He crowns the humble with salvation.
b: This passage shows us how God adorns those who are humble in heart with His salvation. In a world that values appearance and status, it reminds us that the truest beauty and the most lasting adornment are not gold, silver, and jewels, but the salvation God gives, the most precious gift of all believers.

An artist is choosing colors for a statue. He has countless choices, but he chooses the purest and most brilliant color to finish his work. So when people look at the statue, what they notice first is not its shape or size, but its unique radiance. In the same way, when we let God’s salvation be our adornment, what people will see first is what God has done in our lives.

An old woman in a small town was known for her good deeds and generosity. Her clothes were simple, but her love for her neighbors and her selfless contribution to the community won her great respect and affection in everyone’s heart. Her humility and spirit of giving became her most beautiful adornment, more attractive than any outward decoration.

Dear family, let us all pursue this virtue. Do not seek worldly splendor and wealth, but let God’s salvation be the adornment of our lives. When we receive His salvation with a humble heart, our lives will show true beauty, drawing others to look for the source that gives us this radiance.
ah: Psalm 149:4 reminds us that Yahweh not only delights in His people, but regards salvation as the adornment of the humble. This is a precious gift, showing God’s special love and grace toward those who are humble in heart. Here are several concrete ways to practice this humility in daily life:
a: **Lower Yourself**
In your daily interactions, learn to put others’ needs before your own. At work or in the family, when you have a chance to serve others, take the initiative to take on tasks that go unnoticed.
**A Life of Gratitude**
Keep a thankful attitude for all the grace God gives, great or small. This will help us stay humble and recognize that everything we have is a gift from God.
**Serve in the Church**
Take an active part in the church’s service and activities, especially those that need a humble attitude, such as cleaning, caring for the elderly and lonely, or helping the vulnerable.
**Avoid Proud Words and Attitudes**
In conversation and conduct, avoid boasting or looking down on others. Communicate with respect and love, showing inner humility.
**Spiritual Growth**
Regularly spend time in prayer and devotion, seeking God’s teaching and guidance on humility. This will help us keep renewing our attitudes and our spiritual lives.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, we thank You for reminding us through Your Word that humility is our adornment, a grace You specially give to those You love. We ask that You help us practice humility in our daily lives, so that our words and deeds reflect reverence for You and love for others. Plant the seed of humility in our hearts, so that we can show the image of Christ in all kinds of situations. When we face temptation and challenge, let us remember that Your salvation is our most precious adornment. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May God’s salvation be the most beautiful adornment of your life, and may you show this imperishable beauty through your words and deeds. Amen!

v: My soul shall boast in the LORD. The humble shall hear of it and be glad.
b: This passage teaches us that true joy comes from boasting in God, and that a humble heart is the key to experiencing it. When we lay down self and rely on God with our whole heart, our souls will be filled with immeasurable joy.

A little child was playing on the beach. As he built a sandcastle, he did not care whether others thought it was the best, nor did he worry that the waves would come and wash it away. His happiness came from the very act of creating, and from enjoying a summer day in the sun with his family. This simple joy is an expression of a humble attitude: focusing on the present and being thankful for every moment.

This picture helps us understand that when we face each day with a humble heart, not trapped by self and not clinging too tightly to the praise of others, we can more easily feel God's presence and the joy He gives. As the psalm says, the humble rejoice when they hear of God's works, because they know that every good thing comes from His grace.

There was a teacher who taught her children every day with love and patience. She sought neither fame nor material reward; her joy came from watching the children learn and grow. Her classroom was filled with laughter and the energy of learning, and even though difficulties and pressures from outside never stopped, her heart still rejoiced because she was able to serve these little lives.
Dear family, when we choose to boast in Yahweh with a humble heart and to focus on His grace in our lives, we will find that even in hardship and challenge, our hearts can still rejoice.
ah: Psalm 34:2 reminds us that the humble rejoice when they hear of the Lord's works. This verse encourages us to find joy as we seek and practice a humble way of life. Here are a few practical ways to put this teaching into practice:
a: **Actively take part in worship and praise**
At church gatherings or at home, express your thankfulness and worship to God through music and moments of praise, and let your heart sing because of the Lord's goodness.
**Share your testimony**

Share with family, friends and the church community how God has worked miracles and shown His lovingkindness in your life. This not only strengthens your own faith but also encourages those who listen, so that the humble may rejoice in what God has done.
**Serve others**
Look for opportunities to serve people in need in your community. When we turn our focus from ourselves to others and see positive change in their lives, it brings deep joy.
**Keep a gratitude journal**
Every day, write down at least three things you are thankful to God for. This habit will help us stay humble and recognize that all our blessings come from God.
**Listen to and apply God's Word**
As you read and meditate on Scripture, focus on seeking God's teaching about humility and apply these principles to daily life. This will draw our hearts closer to God.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You that the humble rejoice when they hear of Your works. Inspire us to take an active part in worship and praise, to boldly share Your testimony in our lives, to serve others selflessly, to record our thanks each day, and to listen deeply to Your Word and practice it. May these actions increase our humility and our joy. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May your heart rejoice as you boast in Yahweh, and may you find joy every day in humility. Amen!

v: The humble have seen it, and are glad. You who seek after God, let your heart live.
b: This verse reminds us that when we seek God with a humble heart, we will find true joy. This joy comes from a deep knowledge and experience of God, and it surpasses any fleeting happiness the world can offer.

An explorer was on a journey in search of treasure, crossing dense jungles and rugged mountains. Though the trip was full of unknowns and hardships, his heart was filled with excitement and joy at the search for the unknown treasure. When he finally found the hidden treasure, his joy was not only because he had found riches, but because of the growth and discoveries he had made along the way.

In the same way, on our spiritual journey, when we seek God with a humble heart, the road may be full of challenges and difficulties, yet in the process we will experience inner joy and revival. This is not only because of the result of finding God, but because in the seeking our hearts gradually open, and we learn to depend on Him and to experience His presence.

A community worker helped poor families in her neighborhood every day. Her work was very hard, and sometimes she felt discouraged and worn out. Yet her heart often felt a deep joy and satisfaction from serving others, because she knew her actions were putting God's love and compassion into practice. Her heart was revived as she sought God's will, and in her daily life she experienced God's presence and guidance.

Dear family, let us seek God with humble hearts and open our spirits to be filled with the joy and peace God gives. When we do, we will not only find meaning in life, but also find a lasting joy deep in our souls.
ah: Psalm 69:32 shows us that the humble will experience joy, and encourages those who seek God to let their hearts live. It is a beautiful promise about the awakening of the heart and about joy. Here are specific ways to put these principles into practice in daily life:
a: **Seek God's will**
In every daily decision and in the big and small matters of life, actively seek God's guidance and will. Do this through prayer, Bible reading and meditation, and make it part of everyday life.
**Celebrate others' achievements**
Learn to rejoice with others when they experience victory or joy. Cultivating this attitude helps us stay humble and encourages a supportive and caring community.
**Serve and give**
Practice humility by serving at church or in your local community. Whether it is volunteering, charity work, or simply helping a neighbor in need, these actions cultivate humility and joy within us.
**Teach and learn**
Keep learning new knowledge and skills, and be glad to share them with others. As we teach, we learn how to listen and respond better, which helps us grow in humility.
**Keep a positive attitude**
When facing difficulty and pressure, keep an optimistic and thankful attitude. This not only helps us stay mentally balanced, but is also a practice of humble faith.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for giving joy to the humble. Help us seek Your will every day, share joy with others, actively serve our community, and stay positive in the midst of challenges. Give us a heart that is willing to learn and to teach, so that our lives may glorify You. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you find joy in humility, and may your heart be revived as you seek. Amen!

v: The humble shall eat and be satisfied. They shall praise the LORD who seek after him. Let your hearts live forever.
b: This verse helps us understand that humility and seeking God not only satisfy our souls but also bring a deep inner contentment. This contentment goes beyond material abundance and touches our deepest needs and longings.

A farmer was working in his fruitful fields. His labor was physical, but what he gained was more than a good harvest; it was the satisfaction of being connected to the land and a peace within. Every day he worked together with the soil, experiencing the rhythm of sowing and reaping. This nourished not only his family but also his soul.

The same applies to our spiritual lives. When we seek God with a humble heart, we are not only seeking His blessing or help; we are seeking a deep connection with Him, which will satisfy our deepest longings. Just as the farmer found satisfaction through his interaction with the land, we find true fullness through our relationship with God.

There was an entrepreneur who was extremely successful in business, but he found that true satisfaction did not come from wealth or achievement. So he began to seek deeper meaning and devoted himself to charity and community service. Through helping others he discovered a new kind of satisfaction, one more lasting and more profound than the happiness material success had brought.

Dear family, when we learn to make humility and seeking God a part of our daily lives, we will find that we receive not only the fullness we need, but that our hearts will also live and be filled with joy.
ah: Psalm 22:26 gives us a profound insight, emphasizing that humility and seeking God bring spiritual satisfaction and lasting praise. This is not only material fullness, but a satisfaction in the depths of the soul. Here are specific ways to practice this truth:
a: **Practice humility in daily life**
When serving at work, at home and at church, lower yourself, take the initiative to help others, look for opportunities to serve, and treat everyone with the love of Christ.
**Actively seek God's will**
Through prayer, Bible study and fellowship, keep seeking God's guidance and will, so that your heart draws closer to His.
**Keep a thankful heart**
Regularly express thanks to God, and praise Him in both adversity and prosperity, because this strengthens our trust in and dependence on God.
**Share God's love and your testimony**
Share what God has done in your life with others. This not only encourages them but also deepens your own experience of faith.
**Keep growing spiritually**
Stay spiritually growing by joining Bible studies, retreats or any form of spiritual training, which will further strengthen your humility and your seeking of God.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for reminding us through Your Word that the humble will find spiritual satisfaction. Help us practice humility in our lives, in our relationships with others as well as in our relationship with You, and keep a humble attitude. As we seek You, satisfy our hearts, and let us praise You with our lives. Let our hearts live because of You, and let us experience Your endless love and abundant provision every day. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you seek God in humility and find eternal satisfaction in His fullness. May your heart live forever because you seek Him. Amen!

v: But the humble shall inherit the land, and shall delight themselves in the abundance of peace.
b: This passage from Psalm 37 reminds us that true blessing and lasting peace are reserved for the humble. In our fiercely competitive world, this is a counterintuitive message: true victory and satisfaction come from humility, not from strength or control.

There was a wealthy kingdom whose riches came from fertile land and abundant harvests. In this kingdom, the most honored people were not the warriors or the merchants, but the farmers who humbly tilled the soil. They delighted in a peaceful life and in harmony with nature. They did not pursue power or the accumulation of wealth, but in the end they enjoyed the greatest abundance and the respect of society, because their way of life kept the land and the community healthy and stable.

This picture helps us understand that when we live humbly, respecting the land we live on and the people around us, we are actually creating a more peaceful and prosperous future for ourselves and for society. Humility is not only a moral choice; it is also a wise way of living, one that can bring true peace and satisfaction.

In our daily lives, this can be practiced through simple actions, such as choosing to listen rather than argue, seeking to understand others rather than trying to prove ourselves right, or seeking God's guidance in difficulty rather than relying on our own strength.

Dear family, let us learn to stay humble in all things, trusting that God will give us our due reward at the right time. When we choose to serve others with a humble heart and to care for our environment, we will find that we are living in the “abundance of peace” God has promised.
ah: Psalm 37:11 reminds us that the humble will inherit the land and enjoy abundant peace. This verse emphasizes that humility is not only a state of spirit, but also the key to the blessing and grace God gives. Here are several practical guidelines to help us cultivate a humble attitude in daily life:
a: **Slow down and feel the present**
In a busy life, make an effort to slow your pace, take time to appreciate your surroundings and the people around you, and learn to see God's gracious hand in small things.
**Serve proactively**
Look for opportunities to serve in your community. Whether volunteering or simply helping a neighbor, these are concrete ways to practice humility.
**Avoid arguments, seek reconciliation**
When facing conflict and disagreement, choose a humble attitude and seek understanding and reconciliation rather than insisting on who is right or wrong.
**Practice gratitude**
Write down at least three things you are grateful for each day. This helps cultivate a thankful and humble heart.
**Devotions and prayer**
Regular devotions and prayer are the key to staying humble. Through these we can build a deeper relationship with God and keep reminding ourselves to depend on God's strength rather than our own.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for reminding us through Your Word of the importance of humility. Help us practice humility in our daily lives, so that we may inherit the land and the peace You give. Teach us to slow down, to appreciate Your creation, and to serve others in our community. Help us seek reconciliation in conflict and practice gratitude in all things, so that our lives may be a witness to Your glory. We know that every good gift comes from You; may our lives reflect Your love and grace. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you find true peace and satisfaction in humility, and enjoy all the abundance God has prepared for you. Amen!

v: if my people who are called by my name will humble themselves, pray, seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways, then I will hear from heaven, will forgive their sin, and will heal their land.
b: This passage from Chronicles reminds us how deeply God values a heart that humbles itself and seeks Him. When we sincerely bow before Him and show our willingness to change and to seek Him, He not only hears our prayers but also brings transformation and healing.

There was an ancient village laid waste by a long drought, and the villagers felt deep despair. In this plight a leader stood up and called everyone to seek God's help with a humble heart and to abandon their old wrong ways. The villagers gathered and prayed together, seeking God's guidance. As time passed, the rain finally came and the land revived. It was not only a rebirth of nature but also a great healing of the spirit of the community.

This story reflects how important it is, when we meet challenges in life, to humbly seek God's wisdom and help. When we admit our limits and seek a power beyond ourselves, we open the door to healing and renewal.

In our daily lives, this means we need to seek God's face in our work, our families and our personal decisions. When we meet difficulty at work, strain in family relationships, or a moral test in our own lives, humbly praying to God, seeking His guidance, and being ready to turn from wrong paths will bring true change and reconciliation.

Dear family, when we humble ourselves and seek God's face, we will not only find our lives gradually filled with light and hope, but our communities and nations will also experience healing and revival. God promises forgiveness and healing, which is a restoration not only of our souls but also of the environment we live in.
ah: 2 Chronicles 7:14 emphasizes that when we humble ourselves, pray, seek God's face and turn from wicked ways, God will hear our prayers, forgive our sin, and heal our land. This verse reminds us that God treasures those who humbly seek Him. To put this verse's teaching into practice, we can take the following steps:
a: **Take an active part in prayer meetings**
Regularly attend the church's prayer meetings, or pray with family and friends, bringing our needs and our thanks to God.
**Daily self-reflection**
Every day take time to examine whether our words and actions accord with God's will, and when we find a deviation, honestly repent and ask for God's forgiveness.
**Seek God's face**
Grow in knowledge of God through reading the Bible, meditation and other devotional practices, and seek His guidance and help for your life.
**Change your way of life**
When we realize that certain behaviors displease God, we need to make real changes and avoid repeating the same mistakes.
**Serve and give**
Look for opportunities to serve in the community and church, showing through action our love for God and our care for people.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, we thank You for reminding us through Your Word of the importance of humbling ourselves, praying, seeking Your face, and turning from wicked ways. Forgive our sins and heal our hearts and our land. Let our hearts and lives continually reflect our love and reverence for You. Give us wisdom and strength to live out these truths in daily life. In all things, may we glorify Your name. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you seek God in humility and experience His forgiveness and healing. May your heart be renewed as you seek God, and your life prosper through His healing. Amen!

t: Humble Yourself and Be Lifted Up
v: Humble yourselves therefore under the mighty hand of God, that he may exalt you in due time,
b: This passage from 1 Peter reminds us of the importance of humility, and tells us that God will lift up, at the right time, those who choose to humble themselves. It is not only a moral lesson but also a principle of life, teaching us to lay down self-centeredness and trust God's plan.

An architect designed a magnificent bridge. Before building it, he first had to put great effort into the foundation, making sure it was solid and lay humbly underground. The bridge's stability and beauty come from that unseen foundation. In the same way, when we humbly place ourselves under God's hand in life, our lives will be built on a solid foundation, able to withstand all kinds of challenges, and in God's own time reach the heights.

This picture embodies the message of 1 Peter: true exaltation comes from humility at the start. In our lives and careers, when we choose to serve in a low place, not seeking immediate reward or recognition, we are actually planting seeds for future success. This humility enables us to learn, to grow, and to prepare for greater responsibility.

There was a successful business leader whose career began as an ordinary employee at the lowest level of the company. In that position he learned every detail of the business and always kept respect for his colleagues and passion for his work. It was this humility and diligence that finally earned him promotion and made him the company's leader. His rise was no accident, but the direct result of the humility and effort he showed while in the lowest place.

Dear family, let us learn humility in life and trust that God will lift us up at the right time. Whatever position we are in now, let us place ourselves in God's hands with obedience and faith, and wait for His time to come.
ah: 1 Peter 5:6 encourages us to stay humble under God's mighty hand, with the promise that when the time is right, God will exalt us. This is not only a challenge to personal character but also a deep encouragement to our faith. Here are some specific ways to practice humility and prepare ourselves to be exalted by God:
a: Open your heart to receive guidance. At work and in church, seek and accept criticism and guidance from those with more experience, and see it as an opportunity to grow and learn.
Serve others. Take an active part in volunteer work and community service, especially the kinds of service that go unseen, such as helping with cleaning or caring for people in need.
In daily life
Live out humility: avoid boasting, listen more and speak less, and give others praise and encouragement.
Keep a life of prayer
Pray often, not only to seek God's help and guidance, but also as a process of self-examination and reflection, helping us keep a humble attitude.
Acknowledge dependence on God
When facing challenges and decisions in life, acknowledge our limits and our need to depend on God, and so stay humble.
pr:
Dear Heavenly Father, we thank You for reminding us through Your Word that true exaltation comes from humility before You.
Help us learn humility more each day, lay down our pride, and hand over all our thoughts and intentions completely to Your leading. Teach us to keep a humble heart in every situation, and let my life be lifted up in Your time. All glory be to You. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you find strength in humility, and trust that in God's time you will be lifted up. Amen!

v: When Solomon was old, his wives turned away his heart after other gods; and his heart was not perfect with the LORD his God, as the heart of David his father was.
b: This passage from 1 Kings reminds us that even the wise Solomon could fall into temptation and turn away from the faith he had held all his life. Solomon's story reveals to us the frailty of human nature and the importance of faithful obedience.

It is like a captain navigating a stormy sea. If he ignores the compass and drifts with the waves, his ship is likely to leave its course and strike the reefs. Solomon's life was like such a ship: when he was old, he chose to ignore the compass of his faith, and as a result he drifted farther and farther with the waves of life.

In our lives, this lesson of faithfully obeying God is just as important. When we face temptation or challenge, we should recall David's example. When he faced wrongdoing and trials, he always tried to seek and obey God's will. We should do the same, choosing each day in our decisions and actions to stay in line with God and walk in His ways, rather than our own feelings or the temptations of the world.

Let us reflect in our daily lives: are we following God's compass, or are we drawn by the scenery around us and passing desires? Every small decision, whether at work, at home or in personal moral choices, is an opportunity for faithful obedience.
ah: In 1 Kings 11:4, we see that King Solomon, because of outside influences and temptations, strayed from his faithful obedience to Yahweh. His story gives us a profound lesson: even the wisest person can lose loyalty to God by going astray. Here are some practical ways to help us keep faithful and obedient to God in daily life:
a: Regular self-examination
Each day or each week, take time to examine your life of faith and identify any misleading influences or temptations that might draw us away from God.
Take an active part in spiritual activities
Strengthen your faith practice and spiritual fellowship by joining church activities, small group gatherings and spiritual retreats.
Set up spiritual accountability
Find a spiritual mentor or a trusted friend, and regularly share each other's spiritual journey, encouraging one another and making sure you both stay on the right path.
Keep studying the Bible
Grow in understanding and applying God's Word through daily Bible study, so that it becomes the guide for life and the basis for decisions.
Avoid bad influences
Identify the bad influences in life that may lead us away from God, and actively avoid excessive involvement with activities or people that might lead us away from Him.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for reminding us, through the story of King Solomon, of the importance of staying faithful and obedient to You. Give us strength and wisdom to recognize and avoid temptations that might lead us off Your path. Help us stand for justice in daily life and seek and practice Your will in all things. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you remain faithfully obedient to Yahweh in your life, and find wisdom and peace in the process. Amen!

v: Furthermore, we had the fathers of our flesh to chasten us, and we paid them respect. Shall we not much rather be in subjection to the Father of spirits and live?
b: This passage from Hebrews emphasizes that obedience to God is even more important than respect for our earthly fathers, because He is the Father of spirits, and we obey Him for the sake of our eternal life.

A coach, like a father, guides and trains his team, hoping they will succeed in the game. When the team members follow the coach's direction, they perform well in competition, and victory comes naturally. This picture helps us understand that our Heavenly Father, the Father of spirits, looks at our spiritual lives in the same way. When we obey His guidance and discipline, we receive not only present direction but also the assurance of our eternal life.

In daily life, when we face all kinds of challenges and decisions, if we remember this truth we will understand the importance of obeying our Heavenly Father. Whether facing a moral choice at work or seeking reconciliation in a personal relationship, putting God's will first brings deep peace and resolution.

This passage reminds us that just as we respect and listen to our earthly fathers for growth and protection, we should all the more obey our Heavenly Father, for He is the endless source of wisdom and love, and the guardian of our souls. His discipline is not meant to punish, but to guide us toward a fuller life.

Dear family, as we learn to obey the Father of spirits in every area of life, may we also experience the life and peace that flow from this obedience. Obeying the Heavenly Father is not only the necessary road for our spiritual growth, but also the guarantee that we will receive true life.
ah: Today's verse is from Hebrews 12:9. It reminds us that the respect we give our earthly parents should extend even more to obedience to our Heavenly Father. On this basis, how can we put obedience to the Father of spirits into practice in daily life? Here are a few action guidelines:
a: Daily prayer and meditation
Begin every day with prayer, asking the Lord to open our hearts so that we can understand His will. Meditate on Scripture and look for guidance for life in God's Word.
Be faithful to spiritual authority
In church life, listen respectfully to the teaching of pastors and spiritual leaders and act under their guidance, as an expression of obedience to the Heavenly Father.
Keep faith in trials
When facing difficulties and trials, hold on to your faith and trust that the Heavenly Father has His plan and timetable. Even if the present situation is hard, choose to obey His leading.
Serve and give
Look for opportunities to serve others in the church and community, offering your time, talents and resources as a response to God's love.
Teach and share
Share your understanding and experience of God's Word with family and friends, and through teaching and sharing encourage them also to know and obey our Heavenly Father.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for teaching us through Your Word how to obey You better. Give us humble and obedient hearts, so that we depend on You more in our daily lives and seek Your will in all things. Help us show our loyalty and love to You in every situation. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you find the true meaning of life in obedience, and flourish in God's boundless grace. Amen!

v: Be subject therefore to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.
b: This passage from James clearly points out the connection between submission and resistance. When we choose to submit to God's will, we also strengthen our ability to resist evil. This is not only a defense mechanism but also a positive spiritual strategy, ensuring that we can stand firm when facing the devil's temptations and attacks.

It is like a medieval castle whose walls are strong and whose guards are alert, so that no enemy trying to attack can easily break through. The castle's safety depends on the guards' alertness and the walls' strength. In the same way, when we build firm walls of obedience to God in our spiritual lives, no attack of the devil will easily succeed; instead, he will be forced to retreat.

This passage reminds us that submission is a strength and a choice, so that we are not only resisting evil but also actively seeking strength in our relationship with God. When we decide to follow God and live the life that pleases Him, we naturally keep our distance from the devil's schemes.

Dear family, when we face temptations and challenges in life, let us remember the importance of submitting to God. It is not only the shield of our spiritual protection, but also our weapon for victory. By submitting to God, we leave the devil no way to escape, and he loses his footing in our lives.
ah: In James 4:7, we are taught to submit to God and resist the devil, and then the devil will flee from us. This is not only a strategy for spiritual warfare, but also a basic principle for practicing faith in daily life. Here are several practical steps that can help us live according to this teaching:
a: Daily prayer and meditation
Begin with daily prayer and Bible meditation, which will help strengthen our trust in and dependence on God. By drawing near to God, we naturally strengthen our ability to resist the devil.
Recognize temptation
Learn to recognize temptations and sins in life, whether in thought or in action. Once recognized, actively seek God's help to overcome them.
Spiritual accountability partners
Find one or more trusted spiritual partners, share your struggles and challenges with them, and encourage and hold one another accountable as you grow together.
Take part in church life

Take an active part in church activities and service, and strengthen your life of faith through the power of fellowship. In the community we can find support and encouragement against the things that might lure us away from God.
Action and declaration
When facing the devil's temptations and attacks, declare your faith and your submission to God out loud. Use the words of Scripture to fight against lies and temptation.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for teaching us through Your Word how to submit to You and resist the devil. Give us strength and wisdom to live a life of obedience to You every day. When we face temptation and attack, help us stand firm on Your Word and resist the devil's temptations. Let us keep growing in Your love and strength, and we give the glory to You. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you experience God's power and peace in obedience, and may all evil flee before you. Amen!

v: But as the assembly is subject to Christ, so let the wives also be to their own husbands in everything.
b: This passage from Ephesians describes a pattern of spiritual relationship, emphasizing the church's obedience to Christ as a model for a wife's submission to her husband. This is not about yielding to power, but about cooperation and harmony based on love and trust.

It is like a pair of dance partners performing a waltz. This dance demands a high degree of coordination and sensitive response to each other's movements. When one dancer leads, the other follows with great trust and harmony. This is more than following; it is agreement on a shared goal: to bring a flowing, beautiful dance to life. Just as partners cooperate in harmony, the relationship between wife and husband, and the church's submission to Christ, should rest on mutual respect and a shared goal of faith.

In daily life, this means learning how to practice submission in relationships. It is not blind obedience but a choice: to choose to trust, to choose to support, to choose to love. Just as the church trusts Christ's leadership, in our relationships, especially in marriage, we should learn this trusting and supportive kind of submission.

This passage reminds us that true submission comes from love and respect for the other, and it should be built on mutual understanding and growing together. When we practice this spiritual submission in marriage or other relationships, we not only glorify God but also lay a solid foundation for our relationships.
ah: In Ephesians 5:24, we see the church's submission to Christ used as an analogy for a wife's submission to her husband. This is not only guidance for the marriage relationship but also a profound revelation about the relationship between believers and Christ. Let us consider how to practice submission to Christ in church life and at the personal level:
a: Trust and obey Christ's leadership
Just as the church submits to Christ, in our personal lives we should also trust and obey Christ fully. In daily decisions, let Christ's teaching and the principles of Scripture be our guide.
Play an active role in the church
Take an active part in the church's service and activities, and look for opportunities to serve others, showing Christ's love and humility.
Personal spiritual growth
Strengthen your relationship with Christ through daily prayer, Bible study and devotions, and keep growing spiritually.
Practice submission in the family
In family relationships, especially between husband and wife, take Christ's love for the church as the example and build an environment of mutual respect and care.
A Christlike attitude in handling conflict
When any kind of conflict or disagreement arises, choose to resolve problems with the humility, forgiveness and love Christ taught.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, we thank You for teaching us through Your Word how the church submits to Christ. Give us wisdom and strength to practice this submission in our lives, our church and our families. Help us learn Christ's humility and love, so that in every relationship we may better reflect the image of Christ. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you learn how to submit appropriately in all your relationships, so that every relationship may reflect Christ's unconditional love for the church. Amen!

v: according to the foreknowledge of God the Father, in sanctification of the Spirit, that you may obey Jesus Christ and be sprinkled with his blood: Grace to you and peace be multiplied.
b: This passage from 1 Peter deeply portrays our holy calling as believers: chosen, sanctified, obedient. It is not only a declaration of spiritual identity but also a blueprint for our lives.

It is like an outstanding music conductor who can blend many different instruments and voices into one harmonious symphony. Every musician is carefully chosen, not only for skill but because their abilities suit the needs of the whole orchestra. Every note and rhythm must stay in line with the conductor's direction, so that the whole is harmonious and beautiful. This is our life in Christ: carefully chosen by God, each of us made part of the spiritual life by the work of the Holy Spirit, and our obedience ensures the harmony of our lives and the fulfillment of the purpose.

Our daily decisions and behavior should reflect this obedience. Whether facing difficult choices or small matters of everyday life, we are called to reflect the likeness of Christ, and through love, service and humility to show that we are not only chosen, but cleansed and blessed so that we can serve others.

As we act in our communities, and as we interact with people in our families and workplaces, our obedience is not only loyalty to God but also a witness to the world around us, showing the power of a changed life. Obeying Christ means that in every relationship and every setting we are committed to expressing a message of peace and love.
ah: In 1 Peter 1:2, we are reminded that we were chosen according to the foreknowledge of God, and sanctified through the work of the Spirit, so that we may obey Jesus Christ. This obedience is not only submission to God's will but also a response to the salvation we have received. Here are specific ways we can practice this obedience in daily life:
a: Grow in understanding of the Bible
Study the Bible regularly, gain a deep understanding of the teaching and life of Jesus Christ, and make this the basis for our conduct and decisions.
Stay connected to God through prayer
Communicate with God daily through prayer, asking Him to guide our thoughts and actions so that in all things we may seek His will and put it into practice.
Live a holy life

Strive to show holiness in personal character and daily behavior, avoid conduct that plainly goes against the teaching of Scripture, and when facing moral and ethical choices, choose the side that accords with God's heart.
Seek God's help in difficulty
When facing trials and difficulties in life, do not rely on your own strength but depend on God's strength, seeking His help and wisdom so that you can obey faithfully.
Encourage one another in fellowship with believers

Support and encourage one another in church small groups and fellowship with believers, growing together and holding one another up on the journey of faith, so that every member can stand firm on the road of obeying Christ.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for reminding us through Your Word that we are chosen and called to obey Jesus Christ. Give us strength and wisdom to keep growing in our daily lives, to know You better, and to put obedience to You into practice in all things. Help us show unmatched loyalty to You in every challenge and opportunity. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you experience each day being shaped, cleansed and made complete by the Holy Spirit, so that you may obey Jesus Christ in every circumstance. May your life be a powerful testimony to God's good plan. Amen!

t: Obedient to Christ in All Things
v: throwing down imaginations and every high thing that is exalted against the knowledge of God and bringing every thought into captivity to the obedience of Christ,
b: In our lives we often face all kinds of temptations and trials, which may lead us away from God's path. These are not only material temptations; more often they are pride and self-centeredness of the heart. Today's passage reminds us that true spiritual victory comes from tearing down these obstacles and giving our whole mind to God, so that everything in us submits to Christ.

An artist paints on canvas the landscape in his heart. If his heart is full of self and pride, his painting will only reflect the chaos of selfish desires. But when he learns to lay self down, and lets his inspiration come from a pure pursuit of beauty and truth, his work will show real beauty and harmony. In the same way, when we choose in life to obey Christ and refuse the schemes of self-centeredness, our lives will reflect God's beauty and harmony.

When we meet difficulties and challenges, let us remember that our strength comes from obeying God. When we choose humility, lay down our own plans and ideas, and trust fully in God's guidance, God will give us victory, just as He makes those obstacles collapse and turns our thoughts back to Christ.
ah: In 2 Corinthians 10:5, the apostle Paul teaches us how to bring every thought into obedience to Christ, tearing down the schemes and lofty things that keep people from knowing God. In our daily lives, this can be practiced through the following specific actions:
a: Self-examination
Take time each day to examine your thoughts and behavior, and identify anything that may lead to pride or distance from God.
Bible study
Study the Bible regularly, especially the passages on obedience and humility, so that our thoughts stay in line with Christ's teaching.
Prayer practice
Every day, ask God through prayer to expose and tear down the pride and self-centered schemes in our hearts.
Serve others
Through serving the community and the church, practice a life of humility and obedience, turning attention from yourself to others.
Share testimonies
Share with others testimonies of how you obey Christ in daily life, and encourage one another to grow in faith.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for teaching us obedience through Your holy Word. Help us recognize and tear down the pride and self-centeredness that hinder us from knowing You and obeying You. Give us a heart willing to serve and willing to learn, so that in our daily lives we keep seeking Your face and in every moment choose to obey Christ. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May each of us, brothers and sisters, live out a life that obeys Christ every day, and find true freedom and peace in His love. Amen!

v: All the princes, the mighty men, and also all of the sons of King David submitted themselves to Solomon the king.
b: Today's passage takes us back to the era of Israel's monarchy, when power passed to King Solomon and the nation's leaders and mighty men chose to submit. It was a critical moment, because the stability and harmony that submission brings are the cornerstone of a nation's prosperity. It was obedience not only to Solomon but to God's will, since it was God who appointed Solomon as king.

In life, we too often face situations that call for submission, whether in the family, at school or in the workplace. For example, when a teacher shares knowledge in class and students heed the teacher's instruction, this is not only respect for the teacher but trust in the learning process. This kind of submission builds an environment for learning and growth.

Submission is not always easy, especially when we face differing opinions or difficult situations. But when we choose to submit to God's arrangement, as King David's sons and the leaders did, we can create a more harmonious and positive environment. When we submit to the authority of justice and goodness, we are in fact submitting to God, because all authority ultimately comes from Him.

Like a family, when each member is willing to follow the family's rules and leadership, the family runs harmoniously. Each person's small act of submission brings greater harmony and love to the family.
ah: In 1 Chronicles 29:24, we see a demonstration of submission to leadership authority: the leaders and mighty men of King David, along with all his sons, submitted to King Solomon. This shows not only support for Solomon's throne but also recognition of God's will, because Solomon's throne was appointed by God. From this passage we can draw out how to practice submission to leadership in contemporary life:
a: Respect and support leaders

In our workplaces, churches and communities, we should respect and support those who have been given leadership responsibility. This means acting under the decisions and guidance they make, even if at times we hold different opinions.
Take an active part in decision-making
Submission does not mean being passive. We can take an active part in the decision-making process, offer opinions and suggestions in a constructive way, and then respect the final decision.
Pray for leaders

Pray for our leaders, whether the pastor of the church, the boss at work, or the leaders of the nation. Ask God to give them wisdom, courage and righteousness, so that they can make decisions that accord with God's will.
Exemplary conduct
As Christians, our conduct should be an example to others. By showing humility and respect in our submission, we can encourage those around us to follow these virtues too.
Stay alert and responsible

While submitting, also stay alert to unjust and unrighteous conduct. If a leader's conduct goes against the teaching of Scripture, we have a responsibility to express our concern and disagreement in an appropriate way.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for teaching us through the example of King Solomon how to submit to leaders. Give us humble hearts, willing to submit to and support our leaders at the proper time. Also give us wisdom, so that in submitting we keep a just and responsible attitude. Help us be examples of justice and truth in every field. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May we learn submission in every area of life, not only to God's will but also in respect for the authorities He has placed in our lives. May our submission bring harmony and blessing, so that we can grow and prosper in every field. Amen!

v: The spirits of the prophets are subject to the prophets,
b: In this verse, Paul reveals to us the balance between spiritual leadership and personal responsibility. He reminds us that even in the most spiritual matters, such as prophecy, there is a need for self-control and self-restraint. This is a perfect display of submission and order, elements indispensable to any healthy church life.

From this verse we can draw out an important lesson on how to obey God in daily life. Whenever we gather at church, we may hear guidance and teaching from the pastor or leaders. Their guidance should lead us to know God more deeply and to put His Word into practice in life. Submitting to this guidance does not mean following blindly, but humbly receiving their wisdom after recognizing the authority God has given them.

In addition, submission shows in how we manage our words and behavior. Just as the prophet is able to control his own spirit, we too are called to control our reactions so that they conform to the teaching of Scripture. This self-control is a mark of spiritual maturity in our interactions at work, at home and in the church.

It is like an orchestra conductor, who not only needs to understand every detail of the musical work but must also lead the whole orchestra, coordinating its playing through his gestures. Each musician's submission is not only respect for the conductor but respect for the whole orchestra and the musical work. In the same way, in our life of faith, submission to spiritual leaders reflects our respect for God and for His plan in our lives.
ah: In 1 Corinthians 14:32, Paul points out that “the spirits of the prophets are subject to the prophets.” This reveals the balance between spiritual authority and personal responsibility. It emphasizes that even in spiritual matters, everyone should maintain self-control and discernment. Here are ways we can put this principle into practice in daily life:
a: Strengthen personal understanding of the Bible
Through personal and group Bible study, grow in understanding of biblical truth. This will help us, when receiving spiritual guidance, to discern whether it accords with the teaching of Scripture.
