If every student were noisy in class and did as they pleased, the classroom would become chaotic and the learning would be greatly reduced. In the same way, in the church, believers should learn God's Word with humility and submission, so that they can truly understand God's will.

A sister named Xiuli was confused about many Bible teachings when she first came to faith. She decided to learn with humility and submission. Each time she attended Bible study, she listened attentively, did not interrupt easily, and was not in a hurry to give her own views. She took notes carefully, and at home reflected and prayed over them. After a period of time, her faith became firm, and she grew greatly in her spiritual life. Xiuli's attitude of submission and focused learning not only built herself up but became an example for other brothers and sisters.

Dear brothers and sisters, let us learn from Xiuli's example, and in studying God's Word listen and reflect with humility and submission. In this way we can truly grasp God's will and put it into practice in life.
ah: In 1 Timothy 2:11, the apostle Paul teaches that a woman should learn in quietness with all subjection. This verse emphasizes the importance of submission and learning, especially in spiritual growth. Although this passage has its historical and cultural background, today we can learn from it the principles of submission and learning and apply them to our daily lives. Here are some specific ways to help us practice this teaching in daily life:
a: Keep a humble attitude of learning
Regardless of gender, as Christians we should keep a humble heart, study God's Word earnestly, and seek spiritual growth.
Focus on devotions
Set a fixed time each day for Bible reading and prayer, be still in God's Word, and let the Holy Spirit guide our hearts and deepen our faith.
Respect spiritual leaders
In the church, respect and submit to the teaching and guidance of the pastor and church leaders, recognizing that they have been appointed by God to help our spiritual growth.
Take an active part in church learning activities
Join the church's Bible studies, devotional groups and various training activities, learn and grow together with other brothers and sisters, and pursue spiritual maturity together.
Practice submission in the family
In the family, respect and submit to one another, especially mutual support and understanding between husband and wife. Such a family atmosphere promotes harmony and love.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for reminding us through Paul's teaching to learn in quietness and with all subjection. Give us humble and submissive hearts, so that we can focus on devotions and study Your Word earnestly. Help us respect spiritual leaders, take an active part in the church's learning activities, and practice submission in the family. May our lives glorify Your name and keep moving forward in spiritual growth. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you experience God's rich wisdom and grace in submission, and may our lives grow ever firmer in the Lord. Amen!

v: one who rules his own house well, having children in subjection with all reverence;
b: This passage teaches us that as parents we should not only manage the family well but also teach our children to be respectful and submissive in all things. This submission and respect is not merely outward behavior, but an inner reverence for God and respect for family order.

It is like a garden designer who carefully tends every flower and every plant, so that every corner of the garden is full of beauty and order. This garden is not beautiful only on the outside, but because every detail is carefully looked after and managed. In the same way, the family is a garden that needs careful management. Only when we manage with love and wisdom, and teach our children to be respectful and submissive, will the family be full of harmony and beauty.

A father named John placed great importance on teaching his children in the family. Every day John spent time praying and reading the Bible with his children, and led by example, showing what respect and submission are. Once, his son Tom met a problem at school and felt discouraged because he could not solve it. John did not give Tom the answer directly, but patiently accompanied him, searched for information together, and encouraged him to have patience and faith. In the end, Tom not only solved the problem but also learned how to keep a respectful and submissive attitude in difficulty. This experience made Tom deeply understand his father's teaching, and he put it into practice in his life.

Dear brothers and sisters, let us learn from John's example and manage our families with love and wisdom, so that our children are respectful and submissive in all things. Our teaching and example will not only influence them for a lifetime but also fill our families with God's grace and blessing.
ah: In 1 Timothy 3:4, the apostle Paul points out that church leaders should manage their own households well, having children in subjection with all reverence. This verse reminds us of the importance of family management and nurture for the life of faith. As Christians, how should we practice this teaching in the family? Here are some specific ways to help us put this verse into practice in daily life:
a: Lead by example
Parents should lead by example, demonstrating submissive and respectful conduct. Children learn from their parents' conduct, so parents should first be their example.
Set up family devotion time
Set a fixed time each day to read the Bible and pray with the children and discuss the teaching of Scripture, letting them feel the spiritual atmosphere and its importance in the family.
Teach and guide patiently
In daily life, patiently teach children how to show respect and submission in different situations. Use concrete examples and stories to help them understand the importance of these values.
Set clear family rules
Set clear family rules and expectations, so that children know which behavior is respectful and submissive. Handle violations of the rules fairly and consistently.
Encourage with love and support
In the course of nurture, encourage children with love and support. Let them know that submission and respect come from love for them and from hope for their future.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for reminding us through Paul's teaching to manage our families well, so that our children are respectful and submissive in all things. Give us wisdom and patience, so that we can lead by example, set up family devotion time, and teach and guide our children patiently. Help us set clear family rules and encourage them with love and support. May our families be channels of Your blessing, to the glory of Your name. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you experience God's wisdom and grace in managing your family, and may your children be respectful and submissive in all things, to the glory of God's name. Amen!

v: in which you once walked according to the course of this world, according to the prince of the power of the air, the spirit who now works in the children of disobedience.
b: This passage reminds us that once, before we believed in the Lord, we followed the customs of the world and obeyed the evil spirit who rules this age. This way of life plunged us into rebellion and darkness. Yet through the redemption of Jesus Christ, we have been set free and have moved toward light and freedom.

It is like a ship sailing on a boundless ocean, trapped by a fierce storm and losing its direction. The crew, tossed about by the wind and waves, feel helpless and despairing. But then an experienced captain comes aboard, bringing the right navigation tools and knowledge, and guides the crew out of the storm and back to calm waters. Christ is like this captain; He leads us out of sin and chaos and guides us onto the right path of life.

A young woman named Amy was negatively influenced by her surroundings as she grew up, and began to live a life of indulgence. Her family and friends were very worried, but powerless to change her choices. One day she met a sincere Christian friend, who kept praying for her and invited her to church activities. Slowly, Amy felt the love of Christ and decided to change her way of life. She received Christ and began a new life. Today she has not only rebuilt her life but also takes an active part in community service, helping other lost people find direction in life.

Dear brothers and sisters, let us remember that we have been rescued from darkness, no longer following the customs of the world but following Christ's leading. Let us live in newness of life and be witnesses in the light, influencing and leading more people to come to Christ.
ah: In Ephesians 2:2, the apostle Paul reminds us that in the past, before we knew Christ, we followed the customs of this age and obeyed the prince of the power of the air, the spirit who now works in the children of disobedience. This verse reminds us no longer to follow the customs of the world and the enticement of evil spirits, but to obey God and live a holy life. Here are some specific ways to help us practice this teaching in daily life:
a: Continue in devotions
Persist every day in Bible reading and prayer, letting God's Word fill our hearts, guide our conduct, and help us resist the temptation of evil spirits.
Discern right and wrong
In daily life, learn to discern what is of God and what is of the world and evil spirits. Reject the behavior and thoughts that do not accord with God's heart, and choose to obey God's way.
Join spiritual fellowship

Take an active part in the church's various activities and fellowship, learn and grow together with other believers, encourage and support one another, and together resist the attacks of evil spirits.
Cleanse your heart
Regularly reflect on your life, confess sin and repent, and ask God to cleanse our hearts, so that we can stay away from the enticement of evil spirits and live a holy life.
Influence others
Influence those around us with our conduct and testimony, letting them see the difference in a Christian and drawing them to God, away from the temptations of the world and evil spirits.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for reminding us through Paul's teaching that we should no longer follow the customs of the world and of evil spirits. Give us strength and wisdom, so that we can continue in devotions, discern right and wrong, and join spiritual fellowship, encouraging and supporting one another. Help us cleanse our hearts, influence others, live a holy life, and stay away from the enticement of evil spirits. May our lives glorify Your name. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you gain new direction and strength in Christ, be far from the control of evil spirits, and live a life that pleases God. Amen!

v: For as you in time past were disobedient to God, but now have obtained mercy by their disobedience,
b: This passage reminds us that although we were once disobedient to God, because of others' disobedience we have instead received God's mercy and grace. This lets us see how wonderful and rich God's grace is: even when we are in rebellion, He still has mercy on us and gives us the chance to repent and return to His embrace.

God's mercy is like a father who has two sons. The elder son often did not listen to his father and did many wrong things. Although the father was stern with him, his heart was full of love and compassion, and he always hoped that he would turn back. The younger son, seeing his father's love and patience toward the elder, was deeply moved and resolved to obey his father and no longer make him sad. This lets us understand how deep God's love for us is: even when we rebel, His mercy remains.

A man named Reggie moved away from the faith in his youth and lived a life of indulgence. It was not until a friend of his met with trouble because of the same lifestyle that Reggie began to reflect on his own life. He saw his friend seek God's help in pain and finally experience God's mercy and rescue. This inspired Reggie, and he decided to change himself and return to God's embrace. Today Reggie is a zealous Christian, takes an active part in the church's ministry, and uses his testimony to help more people know God's grace.

Dear brothers and sisters, let us remember that however much we have rebelled, God's mercy is always waiting for us to turn back. His grace is limitless, giving us new opportunity and hope. Let us treasure this grace, obey God's will, and live a life that pleases Him.
ah: In Romans 11:30, the apostle Paul reminds us that although we were once disobedient to God, we have now obtained mercy through their disobedience. This verse emphasizes God's mercy and grace: whatever our past, as long as we repent, God is willing to receive us. Here are some specific ways to help us practice this teaching in daily life:
a: Reflect and repent often
Regularly reflect on your life, recognize your mistakes and disobedience, repent before God, and ask for His forgiveness and guidance.
Receive God's mercy and grace
Whatever the past, trust in God's mercy, receive His grace, and believe He will give us a new beginning and let us grow in His love.
Learn to obey God's Word
Read the Bible and pray every day, study God's Word, and let the Holy Spirit guide our lives and help us practice obedience in daily conduct.
Take part in church life
Take an active part in the church's worship, fellowship and ministry, deepening our obedience to God and love for Him through spiritual fellowship and service.
Pass on God's love and mercy
Through our testimony and conduct, pass on God's love and mercy to others, helping more people know and experience God's grace.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for reminding us through Paul's teaching that even though we were formerly disobedient, now through Your mercy we can be forgiven. Give us a repentant heart to receive Your grace, and to learn to obey Your Word in life. Help us take an active part in church life and pass on Your love and mercy, so that more people may know You. May our lives glorify Your name. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you gain new life and strength in God's mercy, and may we together experience His abundant grace in obedience. Amen!

v: For God has bound all to disobedience, that he might have mercy on all.
b: This passage reveals a profound truth: God allowed all to fall into a state of disobedience in order to make His mercy and grace more evident. It reminds us that even in our rebellion and weakness, God's mercy still comes to us, and He is willing to give grace so that we repent and turn to Him.

It is like a doctor who allows his patient to feel some pain and discomfort during treatment so that the patient understands the necessity of the treatment and the doctor's earnest concern. Though the pain is short-lived, it leads the patient toward recovery. In the same way, God lets us experience disobedience so that we may feel the depth of His mercy and so that our lives may be healed and renewed.

A young man named George left home in rebellion in his youth and lived a life of indulgence. His parents and friends kept praying for him, hoping he would turn back. But George continued to go his own way until he met with a major setback and his life hit rock bottom. In that plight he began to think about his life, and finally met God at a church meeting. He felt God's mercy and love, and resolved to repent and return to the embrace of his family and of God. Today George is a pastor, devoted to helping more lost people find their way home.

Dear brothers and sisters, let us remember that God's mercy and grace far exceed our transgressions and rebellion. He wants us to wake up in our disobedience and lead us back to the right path with His mercy. Let us treasure this grace, practice the truth of obedience in life, and be witnesses of God's mercy.
ah: In Romans 11:32, the apostle Paul points out that God has shut up all to disobedience, that He might have mercy on all. This verse reminds us that God's mercy goes beyond our disobedience, and that His grace is to save all people. Here are some specific ways to help us practice this teaching in daily life:
a: Admit your disobedience
Be bold to admit your past or present disobedience, recognizing that each of us has weakness and failure. This is the beginning of receiving God's mercy.
Give thanks for God's mercy
Give thanks every day for God's mercy and grace. He has not left us because of our disobedience but has given us the opportunity to change.
Live a life of grace
Use God's grace as strength to change our conduct and attitude and live a life of obedience to God, so that our lives become proof that witnesses to God's mercy.
Accept and forgive others
Recognizing that God also has mercy on others' disobedience, we should learn to accept and forgive others, treating the people around us with love and patience.
Share God's mercy
Pass on God's mercy and grace to others, and through our testimony and actions help them recognize God's love and mercy, and lead them back into God's embrace.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for reminding us through Paul's teaching that even in disobedience, You still have mercy on us. Help us admit our disobedience, give thanks for Your mercy, and change our lives with Your grace. Give us hearts that accept and forgive others, so that we can pass on Your love and mercy to more people. May our lives glorify Your name and witness to Your grace. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you gain new life and strength in God's mercy, and may we together experience His abundant grace in obedience. Amen!
